skew.title: Stage 9 skewed 11.8x (max vs median task)
skew.evidence: 89 tasks, slowest is 11.8x the median and reads 13.8x the median data - one partition holds most of the data.
skew.fix: Salt the skewed join/group key or enable AQE skew join; a plain repartition will not fix a value-skewed key.

disk_spill.title: Stage 13 spilled 15.8 GiB to disk (136 GiB in-memory at spill time)
disk_spill.evidence: Disk spill 15.8 GiB / in-memory 136.1 GiB over 128 tasks - per-task data exceeds execution memory.
disk_spill.fix: Raise spark.sql.shuffle.partitions (smaller partitions) first; if it persists, raise executor memory.

shuffle_partition_sizing.title: Stage 5 wide shuffle (782 GiB, ~801 MiB/partition)
shuffle_partition_sizing.evidence: 782 GiB shuffle write over shuffle.partitions=1000 = ~801 MiB per partition - oversized reducers spill.
shuffle_partition_sizing.fix: Raise spark.sql.shuffle.partitions to ~3128 (~256 MiB each). AQE coalesce is already on; it only merges small partitions and cannot split oversized ones.

shuffle_fetch_wait.title: Stage 24 spends 81% of task time waiting on shuffle fetch
shuffle_fetch_wait.evidence: 124323s of 152838s task time is shuffle-fetch wait over 587 tasks - the shuffle IO path is the bottleneck, not compute.
shuffle_fetch_wait.fix: Check which executors hold the map output before changing partition counts. If it is concentrated (the map stage ran while the fleet was still scaling up), raise dynamicAllocation.initialExecutors so the map stage spreads its output; raising spark.sql.shuffle.partitions then makes it WORSE by multiplying block count. Raise partitions only when the blocks themselves are large.

idle_reserved_executors.title: Executors 13% utilized: ~43 idle executor-hours held
idle_reserved_executors.evidence: 420 executors held 49 executor-hours but task slots were busy only 13% of that; 48 were released before app end. shuffleTracking pins executors whose shuffle blocks a live job still references, so the fleet is held until the tail task finishes.
idle_reserved_executors.fix: Fix the tail that keeps the final job alive (speculation for stragglers, skew fixes) - releasing executors mid-query is not achievable via shuffleTracking.timeout, which only applies after the referencing job ends.

straggler.title: Stage 2 straggler: slowest task 35.3x the median on uniform data
straggler.evidence: 2999 tasks, slowest is 35.3x the median wall time but reads only 1.0x the median data - a slow executor/node or IO stall, not data skew. spark.speculation is OFF, so nothing re-ran it.
straggler.fix: Enable spark.speculation=true (with spark.speculation.quantile ~0.9) so a straggling task is re-launched on an idle executor instead of pinning the stage.
